why:
phase-492 W1.b: renamed from `rclc_subscription_callback_t`, which is rclc's name for a different contract (a deserialised message, no context); RFC-0089 rule 2 gives this one a distinct name.

RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-13 (phase-417 W5.a follow-through), divergence -> extension. Both halves of the old reason were refuted, one by our own code and one by RFC-0089 itself, and they are recorded here rather than smoothed away.

It said: "the callback is bound to the ENTITY at creation (RFC-0041), so its type belongs to the subscription rather than to the executor's add call. rclc's counterpart is `rclc_subscription_callback_t`, passed to `rclc_executor_add_subscription` -- the `executor-owns-no-entity-storage` rule, seen as a type."

(1) THE BINDING SITE MOVED. phase-417 stage 6 took the callback off `*_init` and put it at registration -- `rclc_executor_add_subscription_raw(exec, sub, cb, ctx, invocation)` -- which is where rclc supplies it. So the sentence describes an arrangement the tree no longer has. (2) THE RULE DOES NOT EXIST. `executor-owns-no-entity-storage` is cited by name in ten ledger rows and is defined nowhere in `docs/design/` (RFC-0089, "RFC-0041 does not decide this, and the rule cited instead does not exist"); RFC-0041's normative content is the DISPATCH MODEL, not a binding site. This row was prose citing prose.

WHAT THE DIFFERENCE ACTUALLY IS, now that the binding site and the invented rule are gone: the DATA contract, and it is the only thing left. Ours is `void (*)(const uint8_t *data, size_t len, void *context)` -- CDR bytes -- where rclc's `rclc_subscription_callback_t` is `void (*)(const void *msg)` over a DESERIALIZED message. Those are not two spellings of one type and must not share a name.

Extension rather than divergence, because the faithful counterpart now SHIPS beside it and carries the correspondence: `c:typed_subscription_callback_t` is shape-identical to `rclc_subscription_callback_with_context_t`, reached as `<Msg>_executor_add_subscription(exec, sub, &msg, cb, ctx, invocation)`. Until W5.a this type was the ONLY delivery shape, so it stood in for rclc's typed one and read as a divergence; it is now the byte TIER beside a faithful one, which rclc has no counterpart for at all. Same verdict and same argument as `cpp:bind_subscription_raw` one language over.

NOTE WHAT DOES NOT APPEAR HERE ANY MORE: "no allocator". W5.a measured that reason and it was false -- rclc delivers a typed message with no allocator either, by making the caller own the storage, and so do we now. The byte callback survives because a caller that parses or FORWARDS its own payload (`packages/testing/nros-tests/bins/bridge-zenoh-to-*`) has no other shape, not because delivery costs a heap. The five C listener examples were ported off it in the same wave, so the byte path keeps only the callers that actually want bytes.
